content: One Breath at a Time, Inc. is a non-profit organization based in Tampa, Florida, established on August 17, 2004. Its primary purpose is to support individuals undergoing lung transplantation at Tampa General Hospital. This hospital is affiliated with the University of South Florida College of Medicine and serves a population of over 4 million people across a 12-county region in West Central Florida. The organization conducts group meetings at the hospital to address all aspects of the lung transplantation process. These meetings cover topics such as the temporary lifestyle changes transplant candidates can expect, techniques to manage anxiety during the process, protocols for adapting to anti-rejection medications, the impact of recovery on families, and how daily activities may be affected post-transplant. The mission of One Breath at a Time, Inc., as stated by its president, Angel Oliva, is to assist lung transplant recipients, their families, and their support systems throughout the transplantation process while also promoting organ donation. The organization has been designated as a 501(c)(3) charity by the Internal Revenue Service for tax purposes. One of the organization’s immediate goals is to establish a Tampa Bay Lung Transplant Home. This facility would consist of multiple small apartments and single-family residences to provide temporary housing for out-of-town and out-of-state patients and their families during the initial evaluation, clinic visits, check-ups, transplant procedures, and post-operative care. This goal is communicated to the public and media through materials distributed by the organization’s directors. The organization’s long-term vision includes the creation of a Tampa Bay Lung Transplant Clinic and Research Institute. This facility would provide patient care, participate in clinical research, and support basic science to advance the success of lung transplantation. Medical institutions collaborating with One Breath at a Time, Inc. would assist in staffing the facility and funding its daily operations. Fundraising efforts are ongoing to support this project. Statistics from Tampa General Hospital indicate a significant increase in the number of lung transplants performed in recent years. The hospital achieved its 100th lung transplant of 2007 in June, surpassing all previous records for the same time period. The organization’s leadership includes Angel Oliva, its president and a lung transplant recipient himself, along with other key members such as Ruth Brakora of Winter Haven, Florida, and Gerald Greenier of Tarpon Springs, Florida. Dr. Mark W., FCCP, serves as the head of the lung transplant program at Tampa General Hospital and acts as the chief advisor to the organization’s board. He provides guidance on the current and future needs of the hospital’s lung transplant program, as well as the needs of transplant recipients and their families. The information provided here was first published in February 2007 and later reprinted in various forms on the organization’s website, which was created in May 2007 and remained under construction as of July 2007. For further inquiries, Angel Oliva, the president of One Breath at a Time, Inc., can be contacted at 1271 Berkshire Lane, Tarpon Springs, Florida 34688, Phone: (727) 430-4969.
